To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have improved the Montgomery algorithm for exponentiation by a factor of about 1.5 in terms of time complexity, and that we have also improved the algorithm for modular inversion by a factor of 2 in terms of time and space complexity.
we propose an improved version of the Montgomery exponentiation algorithm, that we provide figures about the performance of this algorithm relatively to a speed optimized version.
we propose a new constant time implementation of the Montgomery multiplication that is faster than the one proposed by C.D. Walter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
- a constant time Montgomery multiplication algorithm - an implementation of Montgomery exponentiation with no final subtractions.

the following questions: 1) What is the cost of a constant time Montgomery multiplication? 2) Is it worth implementing a constant time Montgomery algorithm? 3) Is there a way to improve the constant time Montgomery implementation?
the implementation of Montgomery exponentiation in a constant time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of cryptosystems based upon modular arithmetic, the Montgomery multiplication should be implemented as proposed in [17, 18].
Montgomery multiplication with no final subtractions is a very good candidate for constant time implementation.
Montgomery's constant time implementation has an overhead of 1.4-2.1 compared to a speed optimisation, depending on the size of the modulus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new version is 10% faster than the original one, and is 20-30% faster than the fastest implementation known in the literature (theoretically).
we have proposed an implementation that is faster, more secure and more compact than the previous versions.
the Montgomery exponentiation with no final subtractions is now the fastest exponentiation method known.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a constant time implementation, the cost of the Montgomery multiplication is not significantly higher than in a standard (non-constant time) implementation.

the constant time implementation of the Montgomery multiplication is not significantly slower than a speed optimised implementation, and thus should be considered for the implementation of modular cryptosystems.
, in the context of cryptosystems, the speed optimised version of the Montgomery algorithm should not be used, as it leaks information about the message.
